subsystem: Work, team, apps catalog, MCP, plugins and skills
summary: The Work page (/work) is a solid task manager: one-line quick add, a Today view, a Board, projects, and a voice/chat 'work' tool. You can hand a task to Apex, and an always-on agent can brief you and pick up tasks, but that agent is off until you switch it on, and the Claude/ChatGPT-plan route has never run on your laptop. Apps (Composio), MCP connections, plugins, GitHub skill imports and Skill Forge are all built and well tested with fakes. Every one of them needs a key, internet, Node/Docker or the master dashboard token before it does anything. One real resident-mode difference: your Python skills are not preloaded, so Apex's list_skills tool shows none of them.

features.name: Work page: projects, tasks, Today, Board
features.what: One place for job, studies, business and software tasks. Quick add understands #area, @project, !high, dates and 'waiting'. Today shows what is overdue, due, waiting and what Apex finished.
features.how_to_use: Dashboard sidebar link 'Work' or open http://127.0.0.1:<port>/work
features.evidence: dashboard/work.py:44-97 (routes /work, /api/work, /api/work/projects, /api/work/tasks), registered at dashboard/server.py:155; page link dashboard/static/index.html:51; agent/work.py:125 parse_quick, :374 today_view; tests/test_work.py (11 tests, passed here); scripts/check_work_ui.cjs
features.setup_needed: None. Tasks live in the long-term memory database.

features.name: Work by voice and chat
features.what: Ask Apex to add a task, read today's list, list open tasks, update or mark a task done, or describe the always-on agent.
features.how_to_use: Say or type e.g. 'add a task: send invoice to Karim fri #job !high' or 'what's on today'

features.name: Give a task to Apex on API credits
features.what: Apex runs research, then coding, then a read-only review, writes the result into %USERPROFILE%\ApexWork\<task>\, and returns the task to 'Review'. It never marks the task done itself. There is a spending cap (default $0.50).
features.how_to_use: /work, open a task, choose 'API credits', press 'Give to Apex' (master token only)
features.evidence: dashboard/work.py:108-122; agent/work.py:438-498 (engine 'api' -> team.submit with config.AGENT_MODEL for every role); agent/team.py:90-133; tests/test_work.py, tests/test_team.py (12)
features.setup_needed: An API key for the model in AGENT_MODEL (.env). It uses AGENT_MODEL, not the model picked in chat (see gaps).

features.name: Give a task to your Claude plan or ChatGPT plan
features.what: Runs Claude Code (claude -p) or Codex (codex exec) signed in with your own subscription, inside the task folder, with a 30-minute limit. Apex refuses to run if the tool is signed in with an API key.
features.how_to_use: /work, open a task, choose 'Claude plan' or 'ChatGPT plan', press 'Give to Apex'. First run Setup-Apex-Work-Plans.cmd once.
features.evidence: agent/work_engines.py:153-210 (sign-in check), :272-330 (run, Windows taskkill /T tree kill, CREATE_NO_WINDOW), Setup-Apex-Work-Plans.cmd, scripts/work_plans_check.py; tests/test_work_agent.py (39, with fakes); tests/test_work_plans_real.py (3) skip unless the real CLIs are installed, so they are skipped here
features.setup_needed: Node.js LTS, Setup-Apex-Work-Plans.cmd, a Claude Pro/Max and/or ChatGPT subscription, internet.

features.name: Always-on Work agent (brief, evening check, nudges, pick up tasks)
features.what: A one-minute loop. It sends a morning brief at 08:30 and an evening check at 18:00, nudges you about tasks waiting 3+ days, and tells you when Apex finishes. If 'work on its own' is on, it takes +apex tasks on your plans, at most 8 a day.
features.how_to_use: /work, 'Always on' tab: switch on, optionally 'Work on its own', 'Check sign-in'
features.evidence: agent/work_agent.py:44 DEFAULTS enabled False, auto_work False; started from dashboard/server.py:63-68 set_agent, which both main.py:411 and app/resident.py:281 call; routes dashboard/work.py:135-159; tests/test_work_agent.py (39)
features.setup_needed: Switch it on in /work. Phone delivery needs agent/notify to be configured. Picking up tasks needs the plan CLIs above, or 'api' added to the order.

features.name: Night shift (overnight coding on a linked Apex Code project)
features.what: Between your evening time and 06:30, an +apex task in a software project linked to an Apex Code project runs as a Safe-mode coding session on a plan. The result shows in the morning brief, and nothing is kept without you.
features.how_to_use: Automatic once the always-on agent and 'work on its own' are on and the project is linked to Code
features.evidence: agent/work_agent.py:340-345 _night, :422-451, :526-561 _night_work; agent/work.py:501-525 stop via code_studio
features.setup_needed: Always-on agent on, plan CLIs signed in, a Work project linked to an Apex Code project.

features.name: Team task workspace (research -> coding -> review -> summary)
features.what: A bounded specialist workflow with a budget ($0.01-$5), at most 16 model calls and 24 tool uses. Coding can edit files and run shell commands through Apex's normal safety checks. Review is read-only.
features.how_to_use: Dashboard > Constellation > 'Task workspace' panel; or ask Apex in chat or Companion Work mode (start_team_task / team_task_status / stop_team_task)

features.what: On startup Apex connects to MCP servers listed in mcp_servers.json, mcp_servers.local.json, .mcp.json, ~/.claude/settings.json or Claude Desktop's config. It supports stdio, HTTP and SSE, and the tools appear in Apex.

features.name: MCP one-click catalog (11 servers)
features.what: Install filesystem, GitHub, Slack, Notion, Google Drive/Calendar, Blender, Brave Search, Postgres, Puppeteer or Home Assistant. Secrets go to .env. It refuses to save unless a test handshake passes.

features.name: MCP permission policy and audit
features.what: Every MCP or App action is classed as a read or a write. With the default MCP_POLICY=ask, writes need your approval. MCP_ALLOW and MCP_DENY lists and per-server on/off switches exist, and every decision is logged.
features.how_to_use: Automatic. Change it with MCP_POLICY / MCP_ALLOW / MCP_DENY in .env. Toggle servers and read the audit in Control > MCP.
features.evidence: config.py:505-511 (default 'ask'); agent/mcp_policy.py:478-504 enforce; dashboard/server.py:2353-2377; tests/test_mcp_policy.py (57)

features.name: Executable plugins
features.what: Install Python plugins from a pinned GitHub commit. A plugin can add tools, hooks, slash commands and memory/context providers. It installs disabled, and you must trust and enable it. Updates disable it until you re-enable it, and rollback is possible. One bundled plugin: session-insights.
features.how_to_use: Main dashboard Plugins panel (plugins.js, index.html:131): paste a GitHub URL > Review > Install disabled > trust + Enable

gaps.issue: In resident mode (your launcher), Python skills are never preloaded. main.py calls skills.load_all() but app/resident.py does not. Apex's list_skills tool returns an empty list, and the self-improvement ledger and curator see no Python skills, so Apex may tell you it has none (email_triage, live_research, publish_website...). They only work if the model guesses the exact name for run_skill.
gaps.evidence: main.py:293-303 (load_all) vs app/resident.py:209-216 (only skill_md.install_bundled); agent/skills.py:80-84 list_skills reads only the in-memory registry; agent/core.py:3342-3343; dashboard/server.py:1365
gaps.fix_hint: Call skills_mod.load_all() in app/resident.py next to install_bundled(), or make list_skills() fall back to discover().
gaps.how_confirmed: Grepped for load_all across app/, main.py and agent/: the only caller is main.py:301. Ran a python snippet: skills.discover() returns 5 skills but skills.list_skills() returns [] before load_all.

gaps.issue: Handing a Work task to Apex uses config.AGENT_MODEL from .env for every role, not the model you picked in the dashboard or chat. Team tasks started from chat use the live model instead. If you switch to deepseek-flash in the UI but AGENT_MODEL is unset (default claude-opus-5), 'Give to Apex' either fails with 'needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY' or bills Opus prices.
gaps.evidence: agent/work.py:456-457 (models={r: config.AGENT_MODEL ...}); config.py:21 default 'claude-opus-5'; contrast agent/core.py:3081-3082 (uses dashboard_server._agent_ref._model)
gaps.fix_hint: Use the running agent's current model (agent._model) as the default, as start_team_task does, or add a model picker on the task.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read work.py:452-460, config.py:21-23 and core.py:3073-3084. The launchers (scripts/run_apex_qwen.py, run_apex_platform.py) do not set AGENT_MODEL. Impact depends on what your .env has.

gaps.issue: POST /api/team (start a team run with a bash-capable coder) has no owner check. A paired device token can start one, while the same action through Work ('Give to Apex') requires the master token.
gaps.evidence: dashboard/team.py:13-29 (only _check_origin) vs dashboard/work.py:99-111 (_owner); docs/WORK.md:44-45 says only the master token can hand work to Apex
gaps.fix_hint: Require request.state.is_master (or no token configured) in dashboard/team.py submit and stop, as dashboard/work.py does.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read dashboard/team.py whole and the auth middleware dashboard/server.py:290-307. Device tokens get is_master=False but are dispatched. tests/test_team.py has no device-token case (grep for is_master/device found only an Origin test).

gaps.issue: 'Give to Apex' on a Claude/ChatGPT plan runs the sign-in check (`claude auth status` / `codex login status`, timeout 60 s) synchronously inside an async route. On the first use and every 10 minutes, the whole dashboard (chat, Companion) freezes until the CLI answers. /api/work/agent/check correctly uses a thread.
gaps.evidence: dashboard/work.py:108-122 calls _guard (sync, :35-41) -> agent/work.py:461 work_engines.check -> agent/work_engines.py:153-180 subprocess.run(timeout=60); compare dashboard/work.py:159 asyncio.to_thread
gaps.fix_hint: Wrap the call in await asyncio.to_thread(_guard, work.give_to_apex, ...).
gaps.how_confirmed: Read the route and call chain. The check is cached for CHECK_TTL=600 s (work_engines.py:47), so the freeze is occasional, typically a few seconds of Node startup.

gaps.issue: With no DASHBOARD_TOKEN, Apps & connections (/api/apps), Plugins/Environment and Apex Home all answer 403 'use the owner token', while Work treats a tokenless instance as the owner. This is deliberate in the code but confusing: those pages look broken.
gaps.evidence: dashboard/apps.py:14-16, dashboard/home.py:14-16 (also used by dashboard/environment.py:3) require is_master; dashboard/server.py:262-263 never sets is_master when the token is empty; dashboard/work.py:99-100 allows tokenless; rationale comment dashboard/server.py:2240-2244
gaps.fix_hint: Show a clear 'set DASHBOARD_TOKEN to manage apps/plugins' message on those pages, or treat loopback tokenless requests as owner consistently.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read the middleware branch at server.py:262-263 and each owner() dependency.

gaps.issue: Skill Forge ('Develop' on the Environment panel, and automatic gap-filling) cannot validate anything without Docker, and Docker Desktop was not running on your last laptop run. Every attempt ends with 'offline validation requires Docker'.
gaps.fix_hint: Show Docker status on the Develop form. Start Docker Desktop before using it.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read the lines. This is a setup dependency, not a code bug.

gaps.issue: The Claude Code / Codex command lines (--tools, --strict-mcp-config, --restricted, codex exec -C/-o/--ephemeral, -c windows.sandbox) have never been checked against the real tools: tests/test_work_plans_real.py skips when the CLIs are absent, as they are here and in all CI. A CLI update that renames a flag would make every plan run fail.
gaps.fix_hint: Run Setup-Apex-Work-Plans.cmd on the laptop. It runs scripts/work_plans_check.py --live, which checks the flags.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read the skip guards. Running test_work.py/test_work_agent.py here passed using fakes only.

gaps.issue: Installing an MCP server from the catalog does not load its tools until Apex restarts. The install returns 'Restart Apex to load this connection's tools'.
gaps.fix_hint: Call agent.load_mcp_tools() for just the new server after a successful install.

gaps.issue: task_skills (task-local procedures) is dead in production: nothing outside tests sets a procedure, so the block the prompt reads at core.py:3820 is always empty.
gaps.evidence: agent/task_skills.py:18-49; grep for procedure(/task_skills.run in agent/, dashboard/, app/, tools/, main.py finds only tests/test_research_learning.py:124
gaps.fix_hint: Wire it to a real caller or remove it.
gaps.how_confirmed: Ran grep for task_skills, procedure( and tasks.run( over production code.

gaps.issue: The MCP config files and the catalog's mcp_servers.local.json are found relative to the current folder (Path.cwd()). The launchers cd to the Apex folder, but starting main.py from another folder would silently load no MCP servers.
gaps.fix_hint: Resolve these paths from the repo root (Path(__file__).parent.parent) instead of cwd.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read the lines and the launcher.

needs_from_owner: Check whether DASHBOARD_TOKEN is set in .env and that you sign in with it. Without it, Apps, Plugins, Environment and Apex Home refuse to work.
Check what AGENT_MODEL is in .env. If it is not deepseek-flash, 'Give to Apex' on API credits will use a different (possibly costlier or unconfigured) model than the one you chat with.
If you want tasks to run on your Claude/ChatGPT subscriptions: install Node.js LTS, run Setup-Apex-Work-Plans.cmd, and confirm it ends with READY.
Decide whether to switch on the always-on Work agent (/work > Always on), and test that the 08:30 brief reaches your phone.
Try one MCP catalog install (e.g. filesystem) to confirm npx works on the laptop on your slow connection, then restart Apex.
Start Docker Desktop if you want Skill Forge ('Develop') to work.
In resident mode, ask Apex 'list your skills' and see whether it names email_triage and the others (expected: it will not, per the gap above).
If you use Claude Code/Codex/Cursor, run Setup-Apex-MCP.cmd to share Apex's memory with them.

rating.why: Work, Team, skills and MCP policy are real, wired and heavily tested, but almost everything beyond the task list needs keys, Node/Docker, internet or the master token and has never run on the laptop, and resident mode loses the Python-skill list.
